text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — saw a short ECC correctable spike across three GPUs on prod-cluster-west at ~01:12 UTC that triggered the dcgm alert and an automated drain. Happened again ~02:03. Looks like fast pulses (30-90s).
Jorge Liu: Which alert fired? can you paste the rule or alert text?
Maya Patel: Here is the alert that fired (from alerts history):
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_Correctable_Active
  expr: dcgm_ecc_corrected_total > 0
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
```
This is the one that caused immediate drain.
Priya Raman: Oof — that rule is basically "any ECC event > 0" with short for. Single transient ECC bursts will spike it.
Tom B.: That explains the false-positive churn. We need a hysteresis or aggregation. Two quick levers: raise threshold or require sustained/incremental increase.
dcgm-bot: [automated] node ip-10-2-4-18 drained by autoscaler due to GPU_ECC_Correctable_Active on 3 GPUs.
infra-oncall: Immediate mitigation: I'm going to silence GPU_ECC_Correctable_Active for prod-cluster-west for 15m while we propose a safer rule.
Maya Patel: Thanks. But silencing is temporary — we should avoid replacing nodes unnecessarily (cost + risk). Proposal: change alert to look at increase() over window and require either multiple GPUs or repeated episodes. Example suggestion:
```
# record per-device delta
record: dcgm:ecc_corrected_increase:sum
expr: sum by (instance,device) (increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total[5m]))

# alert when sum across devices on a host exceeds X OR when a single device has repeated increases
expr (proposal): (
  sum by (instance) (dcgm:ecc_corrected_increase:sum) > 50
) OR (
  max by (instance,device) (dcgm:ecc_corrected_increase:sum) > 30
)
for: 10m
```
Priya Raman: I like the multi-pronged approach. Also add a rolling "spike_score" recording rule that discounts single-sample blips, e.g.:
```
record: gpu:ecc_spike_score:ratio
expr: (
  increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total[1m]) * 4 + increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total[5m])
) / (1 + increase(dcgm_ecc_corrected_total[15m]))
```
Then threshold spike_score > 20 AND >=2 distinct devices.
Jorge Liu: Another idea: require the alert to be satisfied across 2/3 consecutive 5m buckets. Hard to express directly in promql but can approximate with recording rules + for:10m. Or we can use changes() to detect repeated increments.
Tom B.: We should also gate the automated drain flow. Add a webhook gate that checks: "are there ECC increases on >=2 physical cards on the node OR uncorrectable ECC events present?" before calling the drain playbook. This prevents drains from single-card transient blips.
Maya Patel: Agree. Cost note: last two drains cost ~1.1k each in reprovision + operational time. We should log those numbers in the proposal.
infra-oncall: Action items I can pick up now: 1) Reduce immediate sensitivity (silence for 15m done). 2) Open a k8s eviction gate PR to require webhook pass for GPU_ECC_* drains.
Priya Raman: I'll draft a Prometheus rules PR with: recording rules for per-device increase, the spike_score, and an adjusted alert with for:10m and a requirement of multi-device impact. I'll include a canary rollout to noisy hosts only.
Jorge Liu: I'll prototype a small lambda webhook that queries Prometheus for the last 30m and only permits drain if (distinct_devices_with_inc >= 2) OR (increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total[30m]) > 0). Will wire to the drain action.
Tom B.: After implementation, we should run a 48h observation window and monitor false-positive rate and any missed real failures. Add a metric for drains_blocked_by_webhook.
Maya Patel: Sounds good. Please also add node label "gpu.flaky=true" for nodes that repeatedly show single-card pulses; we can exclude them from auto-replace and schedule manual inspections.
infra-oncall: Will add label and a ticket to tracking board.
Maya Patel: I'll open the RFC/PR today with examples and cost numbers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Jorge Liu: lgtm, thanks Maya.
Priya Raman: I'll push rule draft in ~2h.
Tom B.: I'll start the webhook skeleton after lunch.
dcgm-bot: [note] next DCGM exporter release includes metric stanza dcgm_ecc_corrected_total with per-device labels (device_uuid) — include that in records.
Maya Patel: Good to know. We'll use device_uuid to detect multi-card vs single-card.
